title: [ROCm] Replace MI300 TF32 test skips with measured dispositions
body:
Removes 14 uses of @skipIfRocmArch(MI300_ARCH) and one test_cuda= pre-test skip covering TF32-sensitive tests skipped on MI300 by PR #166478, and replaces each with a disposition grounded in numerical measurement.

Background: the skips existed because the tests failed under hipBLASLt's FAST_TF32 (which maps to AMD CDNA3 XF32 matrix instructions) while passing on NVIDIA TF32. A standalone analysis harness at https://github.com/jeffdaily/tf32_analysis characterizes each failure and quantifies the AMD XF32 vs ideal NV-TF32 gap at the GEMM level, confirming that CDNA3's round-down accumulation is a documented hardware property (arXiv:2511.10909), not a hipBLASLt accuracy bug. Each test lands in one of four dispositions:

  1. Vendor-agnostic tolerance bump — when even ideal NV-TF32 exceeds the prior tolerance, the tolerance is wrong for the shape, not the hardware (test_addmm_sizes, test_broadcast_batched_matmul).

  2. ROCm-conditional tolerance bump — when NV-TF32 passes the tolerance but AMD XF32 does not, preserve CUDA coverage and relax only on ROCm (test_compile_kernel_advanced, test_Conv2d_size_1_kernel, test_ConvTranspose2d_size_1_kernel, test_cdist_large, test_tensordot, Linear no_bias module test).

  3. @with_highest_f32_precision — when the test's intent is algorithmic correctness (not matmul precision) and TF32 noise is unrelated or amplified to the point where no sensible tolerance works (test_old_cholesky, test_rnn_fused, the three affine_grid/grid_sample tests). A new unified decorator is added to common_utils.py that calls torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(\"highest\") with save/restore, covering both CUDA TF32 and CPU mkldnn reduced-f32 matmul.

  4. Drop the skip, no other change — when measurement shows the test already passes at existing tolerances (test_transformerencoder_fastpath, which compares fastpath vs slowpath and not TF32 vs FP32; test_variable_sequence, whose tiny LSTM sizes don't dispatch through MFMA).

Review order: start with the new @with_highest_f32_precision helper in common_utils.py, then the category-1/2 tolerance bumps in test_linalg.py, test_cuda.py, test/nn/test_convolution.py, test_torch.py, and common_nn.py; then the category-3 decorator applications in test_nn.py and test_linalg.py; then the pure-skip removals in test_transformers.py and test_nn.py's
test_variable_sequence.

Authored with Claude (claude.ai/code).
